## Approach

**Data**: 300 samples, 16 numeric + 2 categorical features, target 200–713 MPa.

**Model selection** — tested tree ensembles, MLP, and structured linear models with CV (5-fold × multiple seeds, R²):

| Model | CV R² |
|---|---|
| RandomForest | 0.78 |
| GradientBoosting | 0.91 |
| Linear (raw) | 0.84 |
| **Additive: √x + x + x² (elements) + P + P² + P³ (processing) + one-hot, Ridge** | **0.971** |
| Same + element×element or element×processing interactions | 0.96 (worse) |

Key finding: the response is **strictly additive** — adding any interaction terms degraded CV. Each feature has a smooth interior optimum (concave), so the global optimum decomposes into 16 independent 1-D maxima. Verified by differential-evolution on the full 16-D space + all 12 categorical combinations (same solution), and by 200 bootstrap refits (optima stable to ±5 %).

**Categorical effects** (Ridge coefficients, MPa): heat treatment `solution_aged` +119 > `quench_temper` +29 > `quenched` −39 > `annealed` −123; route `wrought` +64 > `AM` −2 > `cast` −61. → `solution_aged` + `wrought`.

**Optimal levels** (bootstrap median; plateaus for weakly-active Si/Cu/Nb/Ti):
- Strengtheners peak mid-range then fall (overaging/embrittlement-like): C ≈ 0.50, Mn ≈ 0.89, Cr ≈ 9.5, Ni ≈ 11.0, Mo ≈ 2.73, V ≈ 0.59, Co ≈ 6.2, Al ≈ 0.64, Ti ≈ 0.58; Nb ≈ 0 (monotonically harmful)
- Processing: solutionizing ≈ 1082 °C, aging ≈ 666 °C, short aging ≈ 15 h (long times strongly detrimental), cooling ≈ 58 K/s

**Validity**: Σ alloying = 35.73 wt% ≤ 100, all ≥ 0 → Fe balance = 64.27 wt%.

## Predicted yield strength

**≈ 752 MPa** (Ridge-quadratic 751.7, Ridge-spline 755.2; GBM 690 — conservative since trees cannot extrapolate beyond training combinations). This exceeds the training maximum of 713 MPa.

Final: C=0.50, Mn=0.89, Si=1.50, Cr=9.54, Ni=11.00, Mo=2.73, V=0.59, Nb=0.01, Co=6.17, Al=0.64, Ti=0.58, Cu=1.58, solutionizing_temp=1082, aging_temp=666, aging_time=15.3, cooling_rate=57.9, heat_treatment=solution_aged, route=wrought
